questions.question: What is the primary focus of Agile software engineering?
options: Delivering functionality quickly and responding to changing specifications
questions.correctAnswer: Delivering functionality quickly and responding to changing specifications
questions.explanation: Agile software engineering focuses on rapid iterative delivery of working functionality and adapting quickly to changing product specifications.

questions.question: Plan-driven development is best suited for what type of systems?
options: Large, long-lifetime systems like aircraft control systems
questions.correctAnswer: Large, long-lifetime systems like aircraft control systems
questions.explanation: Plan-driven approaches are designed for large, complex, long-lived, or safety-critical systems (such as aerospace and defense systems) that require thorough upfront analysis and documentation.

questions.question: According to the Agile Manifesto, what is valued over comprehensive documentation?
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto explicitly values working software over comprehensive documentation.

questions.question: What is the core process around which all agile methods are based?
questions.explanation: All agile methods are built around incremental development and delivery—defining, building, and delivering features in small iterations to gather feedback.

questions.question: Which Agile principle involves trusting the development team to work without prescriptive software processes?
options: Focus on people, not the development process
questions.correctAnswer: Focus on people, not the development process
questions.explanation: Focusing on people rather than rigid processes means trusting the skills of the development team and allowing them to work in their own way without prescriptive overhead.

questions.question: Who coined the name "Extreme Programming" in 1998?
questions.explanation: Kent Beck introduced Extreme Programming (XP) in 1998 by pushing recognized good development practices to "extreme" levels.

questions.question: In Extreme Programming, writing tests before writing the actual code is called:
questions.explanation: Test-driven development (TDD) is the practice of writing automated executable tests for a feature before writing the code that implements it.

questions.question: What XP practice involves improving the structure, readability, efficiency, and security of code without changing its external behavior?
questions.explanation: Refactoring continuously improves internal code structure, readability, efficiency, and security while preserving external functionality.

questions.question: Unlike XP, what does Scrum provide a framework for?
questions.explanation: Scrum focuses on agile project organization and planning rather than prescribing specific technical programming practices.

questions.question: In product development, who should normally take on the "Product Owner" role in Scrum?
questions.explanation: In software product companies, the product manager normally serves as the Scrum Product Owner, identifying features and prioritizing the backlog.

questions.question: Which Scrum role is described as a "team coach" rather than a conventional project manager?
questions.explanation: The ScrumMaster acts as a team coach who facilitates Scrum practices and removes roadblocks rather than managing the team hierarchically.

questions.question: How long does a Sprint typically last in Scrum?
questions.explanation: A Sprint is a fixed-length iteration that typically lasts between 2 and 4 weeks.

questions.question: What is the "Product Backlog" in Scrum?
options: A prioritized to-do list of items to be implemented
A document detailing the system architecture
A log of failed automated tests
questions.correctAnswer: A prioritized to-do list of items to be implemented
questions.explanation: The Product Backlog is a prioritized list of Product Backlog Items (PBIs) such as features, user stories, bug fixes, and engineering improvements remaining to be built.

questions.question: A Product Backlog Item (PBI) that has enough detail for the team to estimate effort and begin work is in which state?
questions.explanation: PBIs progress through states (Ready for consideration -> Ready for refinement -> Ready for implementation); once in Ready for implementation, they have sufficient detail to be estimated and selected for a sprint.

questions.question: What are "Story Points"?
options: Exact hours a task will take
The number of developers needed for a task
An arbitrary estimate of effort evaluated relatively against a baseline task
The priority rank of a feature
questions.correctAnswer: An arbitrary estimate of effort evaluated relatively against a baseline task
questions.explanation: Story points represent relative effort estimates comparing the size and complexity of a task against a known baseline task.

questions.question: Sprints are "timeboxed". What does this mean?
options: Developers track their hours in a timebox application.
Development stops at the end of the sprint whether work is completed or not.
Sprints are extended indefinitely until all backlog items are finished.
questions.correctAnswer: Development stops at the end of the sprint whether work is completed or not.
questions.explanation: Timeboxing means the sprint has a strict fixed end date; work stops when the time expires regardless of whether all planned items are finished.

questions.question: If it is impossible to complete all sprint backlog items during a sprint, what happens?
options: The sprint is extended by one week.
The unfinished items are returned to the product backlog and queued for a future sprint.
questions.correctAnswer: The unfinished items are returned to the product backlog and queued for a future sprint.
questions.explanation: Because sprints are never extended, any incomplete items are returned to the product backlog to be reprioritized for a future sprint.

questions.question: A short, daily meeting where team members share progress and problems is called a:
questions.explanation: A Scrum (or daily standup) is a short daily meeting where the team reviews progress since the last meeting, plans the day's work, and surfaces blockers.

questions.question: What is the ideal size for a Scrum Development Team?
questions.explanation: A self-organizing Scrum development team ideally consists of 5 to 8 people—large enough to cover diverse skills and small enough to communicate effectively.

questions.question: In Scrum, who is intended to handle team-focused external interactions to shield developers from distractions?
questions.explanation: To protect the team from external distractions, the ScrumMaster handles team-focused external interactions while the Product Owner handles product-focused interactions.
